dry-above.author: Murray's Fly Shop
dry-above.shows: Mr. Rapidan Parachute (#16) floating on still water, seen from above: hackle spread flat in the film, tail and body lying on the surface, dimples under the hackle tips.
dry-above.compare: How much of the body and tail lie on the film; hackle fibre spread and their dimples; parachute post seen end-on; colour of the fly against the water.

dry-above.author: Murray's Fly Shop
dry-above.shows: The same #16 parachute floating, low side view with its mirror reflection: hackle and tail rest on the film, body almost touching it, post upright.
dry-above.compare: Body height above the film (about zero); hook bend hangs below the surface; reflection strength and the meniscus line where hackle meets water.

dry-above.author: Nick Thomas (The Global FlyFisher)
dry-above.shows: Foam hopper with poly wing and rubber legs floating in about 15 mm of water in a grey dish; reflection, leg dimples and the shadow on the dish bottom.
dry-above.compare: Foam body sitting in, not on, the film; dimples where the rubber legs touch; shadow and bright caustic rims on the shallow bottom.

dry-above.author: Nick Thomas (The Global FlyFisher)
dry-above.shows: Poly-yarn sedge floating, low angle, with the tippet leading away across the surface; the wing tent sits on the film, a bright meniscus runs along the tippet.
dry-above.compare: Caddis wing lying on the water vs held above it; body in the film; tippet meniscus near the eye (a highlight line, not a dark line).

dry-above.author: CosmicJohn (Box of Rain, Substack)
dry-above.shows: Hackled, winged dry fly on still water at eye level with its reflection of sky and wing; hackle and tail resting on the film.
dry-above.compare: Hackle-tip contact points and their tiny dimples; how high the body rides; hook bend and point below the surface.

dry-below.author: J. Castwell ("Flies Only" series, FlyAnglers Online; posted by Bruce_Norikane)
dry-below.shows: Hackled dry fly photographed from under the surface at a low angle: hackle and tail tips pressing silvery dimples into the film, hook bend hanging into the water, the underside of the surface acting as a mirror.
dry-below.compare: Dimple size relative to the hackle length; bright silver rims of the dimples; how the mirror reflects the parts below the film; hook and body silhouette.

dry-below.author: J. Castwell ("Flies Only" series, FlyAnglers Online; posted by Bruce_Norikane)
dry-below.shows: The same kind of fly seen from more directly below: dark silhouette of body and hook, hackle fibres radiating, tail dimple a round bright-rimmed disc.
dry-below.compare: Silhouette darkness against the sky; diameter of the tail and hackle dimples relative to the gape; hackle fibres above the film blurred vs those in it.

dry-below.author: J. Castwell ("Flies Only" series, FlyAnglers Online; posted by Bruce_Norikane)
dry-below.shows: Dry fly at the edge of the window seen from below: the part above the surface is refracted and stretched upward, dimples flash silver, bottom-coloured mirror below the window edge.
dry-below.compare: Snell's window edge (bright above, mirror below); vertical stretching of the hackle above the film; dimple highlights.

dry-below.author: Gordon Byrnes (Fly Fisherman)
dry-below.shows: Photos 1A-1D: a standard dry fly photographed from underwater (black and white), sharp as a human sees it and defocused to approximate trout vision at 1 ft, 6 in and 3 in.
dry-below.compare: Overall silhouette from below and which parts (hackle, tail, body) read at a distance; blur at range.

wet-under.author: Nick Thomas (The Global FlyFisher)
wet-under.shows: Nymph on tippet photographed under water in a small tank: dubbing and fibres studded with air bubbles, bead and tippet visible, black background.
wet-under.compare: Air bubbles clinging to dubbing and fibre tips (size and count); wet dubbing translucency; fibres splayed, not collapsed.

wet-under.author: Ray Tucker (Flymph Forum, 2009)
wet-under.shows: Soft-hackle wet fly (flymph) on tippet under water: soft hackle fibres separated and swept back, peacock thorax and dubbed body, small air bubbles along the fibres.
wet-under.compare: Hackle fibres spread vs clumped underwater; body colour darkening when wet; bubbles on hackle; hook and tippet angle.

wet-under.author: Ray Tucker (Flymph Forum, 2009)
wet-under.shows: The same flymph under water seen further away, with the water surface and its underside reflection in the background.
wet-under.compare: Hackle sweep and fly attitude on a slack tippet; underside of the surface seen from below.

wet-under.author: Alex Voerman (aviper2k7)
wet-under.shows: Bead-head nymph (Prince-style, white biot wings, brown tails) photographed under water from above and in front, tippet at the eye.
wet-under.compare: Bead brightness under water; biot wings and tails keep their shape; dubbing/peacock body darkness when wet.

wet-under.author: Nick Thomas (The Global FlyFisher)
wet-under.shows: "Fluffy and collapsed": the same orange dubbed nymph dry (fluffy) and wet (dubbing fibres collapsed against the body). Out of the water.
wet-under.compare: How far dubbing fibres stand out dry vs wet; colour darkening when wet.
